name: Duskframe Crowd-Walker Operative Set
description: A deceptively ordinary-looking ensemble built for runners who need to vanish into Tier 2-3 foot traffic. The centerpiece is a reversible field jacket in dusty slate on one side and oil-stained rust-brown on the other — both sides treated with scatter-weave scanner-resistant fiber panels sewn into the lining, making it opaque to standard port and transit body scanners. The jacket's interior is a maze of flat holster channels, zippered tool sleeves, and a reinforced spine channel that routes aug-power cabling from a hip-mount battery pack to shoulder-level chrome. Collar is slightly raised, hiding a folded balaclava that deploys in seconds. Underneath sits a dark teal compression shirt with embedded comm-wire loops at the collar and reinforced left-side panels where a subdermal rig typically presses. Bottoms are a pair of deep charcoal straight-leg trousers with double-layer knee panels and two concealed thigh-pockets sewn flush against the inseam — invisible when standing, accessible with one hand. Footwear is a low-profile slate-grey street boot with silent-tread soles and a magnetic ankle clip that releases a folded ankle holster. A worn canvas tote bag completes the look — utterly forgettable, internally lined with signal-dampening mesh.
functionality: Reversible jacket for quick identity shift, scanner-resistant panels in jacket and bag, interior holster channels and tool sleeves, aug-power routing spine channel, comm-wire loops at collar, concealed thigh and ankle holsters, silent-tread soles
what_it_says: This is someone who has spent years perfecting the art of looking unremarkable. The wear patterns are calculated — scuffs where a transit worker would have them, the tote bag that reads as a lunch haul. Anyone who knows the trade recognizes the jacket's slightly stiff shoulders for what they are. Everyone else sees a shift worker heading home.
worn_by: mid-tier runners who specialize in social infiltration
couriers moving sensitive packages through checkpoints
fixers who need to move between neighborhoods without burning their cover
manufacturer: Ashgrain Collective — street label, Circuit District, unlicensed
story_hooks: A runner in this outfit is stopped at a Kelvex transit checkpoint — the scanner clears them, but a sharp-eyed platform officer notices the jacket's collar is slightly too stiff and the tote bag sits oddly flat. Does the runner talk their way through or burn the exit route?

The rust-brown side of the jacket was last worn during a job that went badly. Someone in the right circles recognizes the specific patchwork repair on the left sleeve — and that person shouldn't be alive.

A client insists on a meeting in a Tier 3 corporate atrium where the dress code is enforced by facial-recognition doors. The charcoal trousers pass, but the jacket's scanner resistance trips an anomaly flag in the building's security AI.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately unremarkable urban operative ensemble designed for invisibility in mixed foot traffic. The silhouette reads as casual streetwear at first glance — understated, neutral-toned, built for movement and function over fashion statement. When the reversible jacket is deployed, it transforms the wearer's outline entirely, creating two distinct visual identities. Overall impression: someone who belongs everywhere and nowhere, deliberately forgettable.
physical_description.fit: Tailored relaxed through the torso with a slight athletic cut; jacket sits comfortably over augmentation channels without bunching; compression shirt hugs the left side where subdermal rigs interface; trousers are straight-leg with a high waist for maximum pocket utility and cable routing; boots are snug at the ankle with zero heel lift.
physical_description.primary_material: Scatter-weave scanner-resistant synth-hybrid in jacket; reinforced ballistic cotton blend for trousers; compression polymer-cotton for undershirt; treated canvas for tote; silent-tread rubber composite for boot soles
physical_description.texture: Jacket outer is smooth with subtle grid micro-texture from scanner weave; rust-brown reverse side has an intentionally oil-stained, weathered tactile finish; compression shirt has fine ribbed grooves; trousers have a slight nap finish; tote canvas is worn and softened
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary palette of dusty slate and oil-stained rust-brown (reversible); secondary teal compression layer; deep charcoal trousers; slate-grey boots. All colors deliberately muted and overlappable with urban environment.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: magnetic snap system disguised as traditional buttons, full-length friction-fit underarm zippers; compression shirt: magnetic micro-clasps at collar; trousers: traditional brass zipper with reinforced anchor stitching; boots: magnetically-indexed ankle clip; tote: concealed RFID-lock magnetic closure
distinctive_features: Reversible construction with dual scanner-resistant lining throughout
Flat holster channel network visible only from inside jacket
Hidden zippered tool sleeves indexed by tool size
Reinforced spine channel routing aug-power cabling — custom welding marks visible on interior seams
Deployable balaclava integrated into collar fold
Embedded comm-wire loops at compression shirt neckline
Double-layer knee reinforcement with silent-flex articulation
Flush-sewn thigh pockets invisible from standing position
Magnetic ankle holster release mechanism hidden in boot heel
Signal-dampening mesh lining in canvas tote — visible as subtle metallic weave along interior seams
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 hybrid: priced and positioned as working-class functional wear, but the manufacturing sophistication and component integration suggest Tier 2 black-market/unlicensed corpo-grade tech. Street label Ashgrain Collective deliberately avoids luxury markers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Designed for runners, fixers, and augmented operatives who move through transitional spaces. Signals someone with corpo experience but rejecting corpo affiliation — a person who understands surveillance systems intimately and has resources to defeat them. Wearing this outfit declares technical competence, operational background, and present intention to avoid detection.
physical_description.condition_typical: New units leave Ashgrain with a deliberately broken-in appearance; oil-stained side of jacket ships with accelerated weathering applied; all magnetic closures are pre-loaded but slightly worn to avoid 'too new' optics; tote bag arrives with frayed edges on handles; boots already show scuff-marks on the toe and heel. The outfit is engineered to look like it's been in active rotation for 6-8 months immediately upon purchase.

image_prompt: Fashion photograph of a lean androgynous model wearing the Duskframe Crowd-Walker Operative Set, shot from a 3/4 angle against a rain-slicked Circuit District backdrop at dusk. The reversible jacket is worn slate-side-out, collar slightly raised with the balaclava partially visible as a folded fabric edge. Moody sidelight from a flickering neon sign casts dramatic shadows across the chest; the compression shirt's embedded comm-wire loops catch a thin line of blue light at the collar. Deep charcoal trousers blend with shadow; slate-grey boots are sharply detailed, magnetic ankle clip gleaming. The canvas tote hangs casually from one shoulder, its signal-dampening mesh interior visible through an open flap. The model's expression is neutral, eyes forward, the kind of face you'd forget three seconds after seeing it. Background dissolves into bokeh of rain and distant corpo signage. Cinematic, minimal color grading, emphasis on function-over-fashion, neo-noir street-operative aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
